items.title: Ruthie Foster interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 28, 2023
items.q: I had one of the best coloratura soprano instructors/teachers at my music school, Lorna MacDonald... She worked with me on range.

ctx.x: I noticed a similarity between you and him, and it might sound a little odd but in the Crescent City video they had some close-ups of you and the way you were using your mouth and your vocal cavity, sticking out your chin, I mean the whole thing. And Joe performed here a number of times and I got to see that, and he did that as well, almost as if he was a trained opera singer.

Oh I got that from him too. Yeah he had a way of moving into his vocal — moving around his vocal range. I’ve never seen — you know I didn’t watch enough of his video to see that. Now I’m going to have to go back and really catch that. For me, I am trained, I am a trained vocalist. I had one of the best coloratura soprano instructors/teachers at my music school, Lorna MacDonald who I think she’s the head of the vocal department, music department in University of Toronto right now. Yeah. She worked with me on…
Yeah. “Every Day I Have the Blues.”
